method.body: A weekly rhythm of reporting and tuning. What got done, what is outstanding, and what needs a decision.

faq.q: Are these four products available today?
faq.a: They are concept and design briefs from the BDS Product Lab, released in build order. VoiceCore ships first because it rides infrastructure we already run; ScoreCore, RadarCore and EmployCore open as new lines behind it. Founding clients are onboarded during the build, not after.

faq.q: Why does BDS sell before it builds?
faq.a: Because a product nobody has paid for is a hobby. We prove demand with a small number of founding clients, build against their real workflow, and only then open the line. It is the single reason our products ship finished rather than theoretical.

faq.q: What does a founding client get?
faq.a: Direct influence over the roadmap, a persona and reporting designed around their business, and pricing held for the length of the founding term. In exchange we ask for honest weekly feedback during the build.

Never as a software licence. Each product is priced against the business outcome it protects — one missed customer, one bad loan, one invisible listing, one role you cannot yet afford to hire. Exact figures are quoted after a briefing call, because they depend on volume and scope.

Sensitive integrations are read-only by default, nothing acts without approval until you switch it on, and every product keeps a full audit trail. ScoreCore in particular is framed under ComplyCore UG so that data handling stands up to UMRA and internal compliance review.

faq.q: Do you work with businesses outside Uganda?
faq.a: Yes for web, brand and marketing work. The four Product Lab lines are tuned to Ugandan financial and communication behaviour first — MTN MoMo and Airtel Money, WhatsApp-led enquiries, English, Luganda and Swahili — and travel to comparable markets from there.
